message.content:
**Uno – Quick Overview** | What | How it works | |------|--------------| | **Goal** | Be the first player to score 500 points (or whatever you agree on). Points come from the cards left in opponents’ hands when someone goes “Uno.” | | **Deck** | 108 cards: 4 colors (red, yellow, green, blue) × 25 cards each (numbers 0‑9 + two of each action card). 4 Wild and 4 Wild Draw Four cards. | | **Setup** | Shuffle the deck. Deal 7 cards to each player. Place the remaining cards face‑down as the draw pile; flip the top card to start the discard pile. | | **Turn** | 1. **Draw** – If you can’t play, draw one card. If that card can be played, you may play it immediately. 2. **Play** – Put a card that matches either color, number, or symbol (action) of the top discard. 3. **Wilds** – You may play a Wild or Wild Draw Four at any time; you then declare the new color. | | **Action Cards** | • **Skip** – Next player loses a turn.
• **Reverse** – Reverses play direction.
• **Draw Two** – Next player draws two cards and skips a turn.
• **Wild** – Change the current color.
• **Wild Draw Four** – Change color and force next player to draw four cards (must be used only if you have no matching color). | | **Going “Uno”** | When you’re down to your last card, shout “Uno!” before the next player takes their turn. If you forget and another player calls you out, you must draw two penalty cards. | | **Winning a Round** | The round ends when a player discards all their cards. That player scores points based on the cards left in opponents’ hands: numbers = face value, action cards = 20, wilds = 50. | | **Scoring** | Add up points after each round. First to reach the agreed total wins the game. | **Optional Variations** * **Stacking** – Allow players to stack Draw Two or Wild Draw Four cards instead of drawing. * **Custom Rules** – e.g., “No Wild Draw Four unless you have no other playable card.” * **House Rules** – e.g., “If you play a Skip on a Skip, the next player gets a free turn.” That’s the core of Uno! Feel free to tweak or add house rules to keep things interesting.
